request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added approvers to the app, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new `person_approver` table (`V87__person_approver.sql`) holds one approver per person. Setting it again replaces it; saving a blank name clears it. The row is deleted when the person is removed or merged into someone else.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/approver`, set up in `approver.POST.yml` with its own small classes. It writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> user=<approver>` to the audit file. The person's details now include their approver.
- **Approval rule:** in `CheckClerkLimit.java`, approving or rejecting a PENDING claim is now allowed for a steward **or** the approver of the claim's person. The existing check in `ApplyStatus` still stops the user who opened or last edited a claim from approving it, approver or not.
- **Front end:** a new Approver column on each person row (`features/approver/approver.slot.tsx`) shows the current approver (`person-approver`), with an entry box (`person-approver-input`) and a button (`person-approver-save`). A refused change shows `person-error`.

**Choices I made where the request didn't say:**
- Anyone who can change the sheet may set an approver; I didn't limit it to stewards, because the test has a non-steward user setting one.
- The approver name isn't checked against anyone's role. The only refusal is a name with a space in it.
- Moving a person to another sheet doesn't carry the approver with them, and merging a person in doesn't pass their approver to the person they're merged into.
